description:
Advances: ancora.review

Severity: High (calibrated). Consolidated findings F7, F33, F34, F59, F60, F61. Found by driving two real generated artifacts in headless Chromium, not by reading templates.

F7 (the High) — Prism destroys the diff markup at load. lib/ancora/review/html.ex:270-278 emits per-line spans classed add/del/hunk_header, then :346 calls Prism.highlightAll(), which reads textContent and reassigns innerHTML, wiping every authored span (295,052 Prism token spans in the branch artifact, ZERO surviving .add). Prism diff grammar then splits each line into a one-character prefix span plus a line span, and .diff span{display:block} at :354 makes both block-level, so every diff line renders as TWO rows: a lone plus or minus, then the code beneath it, with all add/delete colouring gone. Separately prism.css is concatenated after css() in render/1:14 and its pre[class*=language-] selector outranks .diff, so the authored dark panel never applies (measured computed background rgb(245,242,240), black text) and dark-mode readers get a bright light block on a #171613 page. No string-level test can catch this: the file on disk is correct and the damage happens in the browser.
Fix: drop class="language-diff" from diff/1 <code> or exclude .diff from highlightAll(); tighten .diff span{display:block} to .diff > code > span; emit prism_css() BEFORE css(). Add one DOM-level assertion that pre.diff .add still exists after scripts run.

F33 — watched_card/1 at :199-202 hardcodes class="badge error", so an :acknowledged badge renders in error red (confirmed on the artifact), contradicting the "drift or acknowledged badge" requirement. Derive the class from card.badge.
F34 — per-finding severity is colour-only: finding/1 at :283-293 turns the severity atom into a CSS class and never into text, and .error/.warning/.info differ only in colour. The Introduced panel is 39 chips of which 20+ read change/uncovered_file with nothing to tell them apart until each details block is expanded, and finding.file is already in the view model but never rendered. Put the severity word and the file into the summary and add a non-colour marker. Contrast itself measured fine (4.78:1 and 4.97:1 light, 9.38:1 dark), so this is colour-as-sole-carrier, not contrast.
F59 — drop role="tablist" (the smaller honest change) or complete the contract with role=tab, aria-selected, aria-controls, role=tabpanel.
F60 — render generated_at in the overview and put the head ref into the <title>; the data is already in the view model.
F61 — add code{overflow-wrap:anywhere}.

Sibling: the 8x diff duplication and its duplicate-id knock-on are ancora-gqb, which also needs a contract line to exist first.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.review in test/ancora/review_test.exs and test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs; one browser-level check that pre.diff .add survives script execution, run through playwright-cli (the playwright-browse skill) against a generated artifact and recorded in the IMPLEMENTED comment, since ExUnit cannot execute Prism
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) diff blocks are excluded from Prism.highlightAll (drop class=language-diff or scope the call) and the authored add/del spans survive in a real browser; (2) .diff span{display:block} is tightened to .diff > code > span; (3) prism_css() is emitted before css() so the authored dark panel wins; (4) watched_card badge class derives from card.badge; (5) each finding summary carries the severity word, the file, and a non-colour marker; (6) role=tablist is dropped or the tab contract is completed; (7) generated_at is rendered and the head ref is in <title>; (8) code{overflow-wrap:anywhere} is present; each of (1)-(3) and (5)-(8) also has a string-level guard test so a regression fails in CI
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a generated artifact keeps its add/del colouring in a browser, badges reflect card.badge, and severity is readable without colour.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/review/html.ex, lib/ancora/review.ex (view-model fields already computed; no scoping change), lib/ancora/markdown.ex
- test/ancora/review_test.exs, test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs, test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement/scenario updates that clear drift/growth/shrink for this ticket's own changes; never weakening a must)

- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Out of Scope (files):
- priv/spec_review_assets/** (ancora-xla.8 pins and upgrades them)
- lib/ancora/review/spec_diff.ex, lib/ancora/review/findings_delta.ex (ancora-xla.6 deletes)
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/gate*

Out of Scope (intent):
- no change to which files or subjects appear in the artifact (ancora-gqb)
- no extractor swap (ancora-xla.9 F17)
- no print stylesheet (dropped by the review)

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

TEST_CRITIC: PASS Session: adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5 Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5.jsonl Scope: test/ancora/review_test.exs in b717ba4 against 7511407. Read the diff, the whole module, test/support/ancora_case.exs, and the finding/1 call graph in lib/ancora/review/html.ex. Ran `mix test test/ancora/review_test.exs`: 8 tests, 0 failures, async. Assertion quality: load-bearing, and stronger than the verifier credited in one place. test/ancora/review_test.exs:44 asserts the exact prefix `
`. That pins the code element as bare AND the authored span as its first child, so it fails if a language class is added to either the pre or the code, whatever the class is named. The refute on :45 is belt-and-braces on top of that, not the sole guard. The badge assertion at :193 pins `class="badge acknowledged">acknowledged`, which fails on a return to the hardcoded `error`. The ordering, CSS-rule and overflow-wrap assertions each pin one authored rule and nothing else.

Brittleness: acceptable, with one over-specification. The three ~110-char strings at :67-74 pin class names, attribute order, the single separating space, and `aria-hidden="true"`. Most of that is contract: aria-hidden is the a11y claim that the marker is decorative, and the adjacency is the reading order. The glyphs are not. `!`, `~` and `i` are styling choices, so a designer swapping one fails CI with no semantic change. I would assert that a marker is present and differs per severity rather than pin the character. Minor, not a blocker.

Ordering test: it proves emission order, not cascade precedence, and the name overclaims. I checked the marker uniqueness rather than assume it: `pre[class*=language-]` occurs exactly once in priv/spec_review_assets/prism.css and zero times in prism.min.js, so the first-occurrence comparison at :49-51 is unambiguous and flipping prism_css() back after css() flips it and fails. As a guard on the ticket's behaviour (3) it is correct. But document order only settles ties between equal-specificity rules, and prism's `pre[class*=language-]` is 0-1-1 against `.diff` at 0-1-0, so prism would still win if it ever matched again. What actually stops it is that the pre no longer carries a language class. The reordering is defence in depth, correctly asserted, misleadingly named "lets review CSS win".

Escaping seam: I would close this one as a non-issue rather than ask for a change. head_ref comes from `git rev-parse HEAD` at lib/ancora/review.ex:347 and falls back to the literal string HEAD, so it is always hex or that word. There is no reachable input where dropping escape/1 around it changes the output, and the fixture value abc123 is honest data matching the production shape. base_ref is user-supplied and is escaped without an escaping assertion, but that predates this diff.

Unreachable clause: agree it is unreachable, disagree that a test is the remedy. Ancora.Finding.severity at lib/ancora/finding.ex:20 admits :off and severity_marker/1 covers three of four, so the function is partial where the type is total. A test for :off would assert a FunctionClauseError, which is a behaviour nobody wants. The cheap fix is a catch-all clause returning a neutral glyph, after which no test is owed. As it stands the ticket's every-conditional-clause check is satisfied, since all three existing clauses are exercised at :67-74 including the nil-file path.

Regression coverage beyond the literal language-diff refute: markup routes are covered by :44 as described above, including `
`, which the refute alone would miss. The uncovered route is JavaScript. interaction_js still calls `Prism.highlightAll()` unconditionally, and nothing in the suite fails if that becomes highlightAllUnder or gains an autoloader. ExUnit cannot execute Prism so no string test closes that fully. One cheap document-wide invariant would catch every remaining markup route at once: `refute html =~ ~s(class="language-)`. I verified that literal appears zero times in prism.min.js and zero times in the render, and that it does not collide with the `[class*=language-]` selectors asserted at :22. Worth adding on a follow-up.

Fixture hygiene: clean. `use Ancora.TestCase` defaults to async: true at test/support/ancora_case.exs:8. Each test gets its own root under System.tmp_dir with a cross-VM unique suffix, removed in on_exit at :31-38, so one temp repo per test and nothing shared. All three new or edited assertions in the first three tests are pure renderer calls that touch no filesystem. Verdict rationale: every one of the eight behaviours has a string guard that fails on a straight regression, the guards target authored output rather than internals, and the fixtures are per-test and async-safe. The two things the tests genuinely cannot prove, cascade precedence and a JS-side route back into Prism highlighting, are both outside what ExUnit can reach and are the exact things the browser proof in the verifier comment covers. Recorded because the gate was nearly met and then actually met, rather than assumed. The Elixir test-quality clause was the one outstanding condition and it was NOT waved through: the diff makes assertional edits to test/ancora/review_test.exs, and a missing critic record is a condition unmet rather than satisfied. The critic ran and returned PASS on its own reading.

The critic strengthened two of the verifier's advisory notes rather than merely echoing them, which is the point of running it. It found the regression guard is stronger than the verifier credited: the assertion at review_test.exs:44 pins the exact prefix with a bare code element, so it fails if ANY language class is added to either the pre or the code, whatever that class is named, not just the literal language-diff the refute covers. It closed the escaping concern as unreachable rather than leaving it open, having traced head_ref to git rev-parse with a literal HEAD fallback. And it disagreed usefully on the unreachable severity clause: a test asserting a FunctionClauseError is a behaviour nobody wants, so the cheap fix is a catch-all clause, after which no test is owed.

Three advisory concerns carried forward, none blocking:

2. The ordering test proves emission order, not cascade precedence, and its name overclaims. What actually prevents Prism winning is that the pre no longer carries a language class; the reordering is defence in depth. Correctly asserted, misleadingly named.
3. One cheap document-wide invariant would close every remaining markup route at once: refute html =~ class="language-.
